issues.description: nevra[0] is wrong when the filename starts with a digit or punctuation, sending packages to the wrong subdirectory
issues.detail: Koji's Packages layout uses the first letter of the package NAME, not the first character of the NEVRA filename. Plenty of Fedora packages start with digits (389-ds-base, 7zip) or are otherwise quirky. nevra[0].lower() on '389-ds-base-...rpm' yields '3', which is actually correct here, but you never validated that. Parse the name properly.

issues.description: Silent None return from extract_arch_from_url produces a malformed URL with the literal string 'None' in the path
issues.detail: If the regex misses, you return None, then build '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. No exception, no log, just a broken lockfile that ships. Either raise, or skip the URL with a loud error. 'else: return None' followed by string-formatting the result is exactly the kind of defensive-but-useless code that wastes the next maintainer's day.

issues.description: Race condition with koji-tagger is acknowledged in the commit message and then shipped anyway with no mitigation
issues.detail: You wrote it down: the URL is fabricated before the tag exists. 'It's safe' because some other system will eventually catch up is not safety, it's hope. At minimum add a retry/verify step, or a comment in the code (not just the commit) so the next person debugging a 404 finds it in five seconds instead of five hours.

issues.description: Hardcoded arch list and koji base URL belong in a constant at module top, not buried in function bodies
issues.detail: Two functions, two places that need to agree on what 'coreos-pool' means. Pull koji_url_base and the arch list to module-level constants. When the koji path changes (and it will), one edit instead of a grep. Small thing; matters for the maintainer six years from now.

issues.description: Stale comment block removed but the 'Prioritize the url from fedora-coreos-pool' logic above it is now largely dead weight
issues.detail: query_packages_location still does the prioritize-coreos-pool dance, but use_koji_url_only rewrites everything downstream anyway. Either the prioritization still matters (say why in a comment) or it's vestigial and should go. Don't leave both halves of a half-finished refactor in the tree.

issues.description: No tests, no way to test locally, by author's own admission
issues.detail: Commit message says 'rpms.lock.yaml changes cannot be tested locally.' Fine for Konflux-only today, but a unit test for use_koji_url_only and extract_arch_from_url is fifteen lines and would have caught the nevra[0] and None-arch issues. Write the test.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The approach is reasonable — give up on dnf5's broken baseurl and synthesize the koji path yourself — but the execution has two real defects: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and lets you format 'None' into a URL, and the Packages/letter subdirectory uses nevra[0] which conflates filename-first-char with name-first-letter (works by accident today, breaks the day a maintainer touches it). The race condition with coreos-koji-tagger is documented in the commit message and then shipped with no mitigation in the code itself. Pull the hardcoded constants up, add a unit test for the two new functions, and decide whether the old prioritize-coreos-pool branch is still load-bearing or vestigial.
